summary: Supplement to the accepted FF.3 algorithm plan: normalized squarefree-square decomposition, exact monic and degree-pair polynomial counts for Bergström–Faber–Payne, and the degree-zero prescribed-coefficient exception in BKK. The prime-polynomial bounds and all factorization, lifting and elliptic counting algorithms are imported unchanged by existing node ids. Explicit requests retain the executable/cost/certificate services and add the all-extension WC.5 point-count bounds; foreign duplication and stage-edge corrections are proposed without editing another job.

nodes.title: Monic squarefree polynomials of degree n
nodes.statement: monicSquarefreeOfDegree F n is the finite subset of monicOfDegree F n consisting of the polynomials satisfying Mathlib Squarefree. Write s_n for its cardinality. In particular 1 is included at n=0, while 0 is never included. Squarefree is the factor-multiplicity condition, not a nonzero-derivative shortcut.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: Filter the accepted monicOfDegree census by Squarefree, using classical decidability.
Membership is exactly monicity, degree n and Squarefree; over a finite field use PerfectField.separable_iff_squarefree to compare with separability.
acceptance: The unit 1 is squarefree, so s_0=1.
Over F_2 the monic squarefree quadratics are X²+X and X²+X+1; X²+1 is excluded.

nodes.title: Unique normalized squarefree-square decomposition
nodes.statement: For every monic f over F, there is exactly one pair (h,m) of monic polynomials such that Squarefree h and f=h m². For this pair, natDegree f = natDegree h + 2 natDegree m. This includes f=1 with (h,m)=(1,1). Scaling this theorem by the nonzero leading coefficient yields the source decomposition for nonmonic nonzero inputs; that consequence is used inside the P_g proof rather than introduced as another declaration.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: Existence starts from Mathlib exists_sq_mul_squarefree, or from the parent canonical square-free decomposition: retain each monic irreducible once when its exponent is odd and use half its exponent in m.
Normalize the square factor to be monic and absorb its unit squared into h. For monic f the remaining h is monic.

Use normalizedFactors_mul and normalizedFactors_pow: for each monic irreducible π, v_π(f)=v_π(h)+2v_π(m), with v_π(h)∈{0,1} by squarefree_iff_nodup_normalizedFactors. Parity fixes both multiplicities. Products reconstruct the normalized polynomials, so both components are equal.
Monic.natDegree_mul and Monic.natDegree_pow give the degree equation.
acceptance: Over F_2: X²(X+1) has pair (X+1,X).
In every characteristic (X+1)^4 has pair (1,(X+1)²).
h and m need not be coprime: X³ has pair (X,X).

sources.match: The source asserts squarefree times a monic square. The proof normalizes both factors for monic inputs using existing UFD results; no new generic decomposition is planned.

nodes.title: Degree-indexed squarefree-square equivalence
nodes.statement: There is an equivalence from the disjoint union over 0≤j≤⌊n/2⌋ of monicSquarefreeOfDegree F (n−2j) × monicOfDegree F j to monicOfDegree F n. It sends (j,h,m) to h m²; its inverse uses the unique normalized decomposition, with j=deg m. Each finite set is read as its subtype. The subtraction n−2j is valid because the index enforces 2j≤n.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: Use the normalized uniqueness theorem to recover h,m and j from f.
Use the degree formula to show j≤n/2 and deg h=n−2j.
The map and inverse cancel by normalized uniqueness; all finite indexing choices are explicit.
acceptance: At n=0 the source is a singleton (j=0,h=1,m=1).
At n=2 over F_2 the source has two squarefree quadratics at j=0 and two monic linear square factors at j=1, giving all four monic quadratics.

sources.match: The exact-degree decomposition supplies the coefficient recurrence behind the degree-pair recurrence on p. 8.

nodes.title: Squarefree census convolution
nodes.statement: For every n≥0, q^n = Σ_{j=0}^{⌊n/2⌋} s_{n−2j} q^j, where s_k=#monicSquarefreeOfDegree F k. This counts all monic degree-n polynomials, not only squarefree inputs.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: Take finite cardinalities of squarefreeSquareEquiv.
Cardinality of the j-th product is s_{n−2j} times #monicOfDegree F j=s_{n−2j}q^j; cardinality of the target is q^n.
acceptance: For n=1: q=s_1.
For n=2 over F_2: 4=2+2, including both monic squares.

sources.match: The source degree-pair induction is resolved into its monic exact-degree convolution, valid in every characteristic.

nodes.title: Exact squarefree polynomial count
nodes.statement: For a finite field F of cardinality q, s_0=1, s_1=q, and s_n=q^n−q^(n−1) for n≥2. In natural numbers the difference is nonnegative, since q≥2. This is valid for all finite fields, including characteristic 2; only the hyperelliptic-curve interpretation in BFP §5 uses odd q.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: The convolution at n=0,1 gives s_0=1,s_1=q.
For n≥2, the j≥1 terms of the convolution are q times the convolution at n−2. Thus q^n=s_n+q·q^(n−2)=s_n+q^(n−1).
Deduce the natural-number difference; q≥2 ensures no truncation changes the integer identity.
acceptance: Over F_2, degrees 0 through 5 give 1,2,2,4,8,16.
Over F_3, degrees 0 through 4 give 1,3,6,18,54.
The generic expression q^n−q^(n−1) must not be used at n=1.

sources.match: The finite recurrence proves the monic constituent of the source degree-pair count without an odd-characteristic assumption.

nodes.title: Squarefree polynomials of adjacent odd and even degree
nodes.statement: hyperellipticPolynomials F g (P_g) is the finite set of all squarefree polynomials of degree 2g+1 or 2g+2 with nonzero leading coefficient, without requiring monicity. Construct it as the image of F× times the disjoint union of the two monic squarefree sets under (a,h)↦C(a)h. Every element has a unique leading-coefficient/monic-factor representation. The definition is a polynomial presentation space, not a set of isomorphism classes of curves; no automorphism quotient is taken.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: Form the finite union of monic squarefree sets of degrees 2g+1 and 2g+2; different degrees make it disjoint.
Scale by nonzero a∈F. Multiplication by a unit preserves Squarefree, degree and roots. Recover a as the leading coefficient and h as normalize f to prove uniqueness.
The scalar action of F× preserves P_g; a field isomorphism transports P_g coefficientwise.
acceptance: At g=0 over F_2, P_0 has four elements.
At g=0 over F_3, P_0 has 18 elements; the monic-only version has 9.

sources.match: This is exactly the source P_g; both degrees and every nonzero leading coefficient must be retained.

api.name: mem_hyperellipticPolynomials
api.statement: f ∈ P_g iff Squarefree f and (natDegree f=2g+1 or natDegree f=2g+2).

api.name: hyperellipticPolynomials_leadingCoeff_ne_zero
api.statement: Every f∈P_g has nonzero leading coefficient.

api.name: hyperellipticPolynomials_normalize
api.statement: For f∈P_g, normalize f lies in the degree-pair monic squarefree union and f=C(leadingCoeff f)·normalize f.

api.name: hyperellipticPolynomials_scalar_iff
api.statement: For a≠0, C(a)f∈P_g iff f∈P_g; the action obeys the multiplication and identity laws.

nodes.title: Count of the squarefree hyperelliptic presentation space
nodes.statement: #P_g=(q−1)(s_{2g+1}+s_{2g+2}). Consequently #P_0=q²(q−1), and #P_g=(q−1)(q^(2g+2)−q^(2g)) for g≥1. Both degrees and all nonzero leading coefficients are counted. These polynomial counts hold in characteristic 2 as well; they do not assert the same y²=f curve parametrization there.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: The unique scalar/monic representation in P_g makes its cardinality (#F×) times the sum of the two monic counts; #F×=q−1.
At g=0 insert s_1=q and s_2=q²−q.
At g≥1 insert the formula at both degrees: the q^(2g+1) terms cancel, leaving q^(2g+2)−q^(2g).
acceptance: Replacing the g=0 count by the g≥1 expression gives 16 over F_3, so the boundary test detects the error.

sources.match: The normalized finite-set argument proves the displayed count, separating its exceptional g=0 case.

nodes.title: Monic coefficient fiber including degree zero
nodes.statement: For n≥0 and b∈F, #{f∈monicOfDegree F n : f(0)=b} equals 1 if n=0 and b=1, equals 0 if n=0 and b≠1, and equals q^(n−1) if n≥1. This is a count of all monic polynomials, not of irreducible polynomials. For BKK Lemma 3.2, use the exceptional indicator when its auxiliary factor degree m=0; the irreducible-factor count still uses the distinct parent fixed-constant theorem and requires nonzero prescribed constant.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q = #F; n,g ∈ ℕ. All polynomials use Mathlib Polynomial F.
proofSteps: At degree zero the parent monic set is {1}.
At degree n≥1, the constant coefficient is fixed and the other n−1 lower coefficients are arbitrary. Restrict the parent coefficient-vector parametrization and take cardinalities.
acceptance: Over F_3 and n=0 the count is 1 at b=1 and 0 at b=0,2.
For n=1 each b occurs exactly once, including b=0.
For n=2 over F_3 every constant coefficient occurs 3 times.

requests.need: The algebraic cost model over a commutative ring R, with the randomness model, as Shoup uses them in Chapter 20 (§§3.2, 9.1, 17.1): (1) an algorithm over R is a program whose primitive steps are +, −, ×, the equality test, inversion of units and, for finite R, drawing a uniformly random element of R, each of unit cost ('operations in R'); (2) a deterministic program's cost on an input is the number of primitive steps; a randomized program on an input has an output distribution (a Mathlib PMF) and a cost random variable, halts with probability 1 when P[more than n steps] → 0, and has expected cost E[cost] (Shoup §9.1.2); serial composition, conditionals and loops (Shoup Examples 9.1-9.4) and the generate-and-test theorem (Shoup Theorem 9.3: geometric number of iterations, E[Z] = E[Z₁]/P[H₁], conditional output law); (3) the dense coefficient-vector representation of R[X] with the costs of Shoup Theorem 17.1 (± in O(len g + len h), × in O(len g · len h), division with remainder by h with unit leading coefficient in O(len h · len q)), arithmetic in R[X]/(f) (+ in O(ℓ), × in O(ℓ²), α^e with O(len e) multiplications, Shoup p. 467), Euclid and extended Euclid over a field in O(len g · len h) (Theorems 17.3, 17.5), and Gaussian elimination over a field computing the reduced row echelon form, the rank and a basis of the row null space of an m × n matrix in O(mn(m + n)) operations (Shoup §14.4, pp. 390-393); (4) the translation to bit operations for the standard presentations of 𝔽_q (ℤ/p, or 𝔽_p[X]/(φ) with φ irreducible of degree w; FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.0), where one operation in 𝔽_q costs O(len(q)²) bit operations (Shoup Chapter 20 introduction), and for ℤ/p^kℤ, O(len(p^k)²).

Executable presentations with refinement lemmas: dense coefficient-list presentations of F[X] over the FF.0 standard presentations of finite fields and of (ℤ/p^kℤ)[X], with lemmas identifying their +, ×, division by a monic polynomial, gcd and extended gcd, and modular powering with Mathlib's Polynomial operations, so that FF.3's checkers (FactorizationCertificate.check, PointCountCertificate.check, FF.0's Rabin checker) and algorithms evaluate by computation on concrete inputs. FF.3's objects are Mathlib functions on Polynomial F; CN.0 owns their computable refinements.

Import the finite-verification certificate discipline used by the parent FF.5: for a finite set S and decidable P, certify ∀x∈S, P x by kernel evaluation of an explicitly checked finite computation, and report verification cost. FF.3 supplies the factorization and point-count checker semantics and soundness; CN.0 supplies executable refinements. CN.5 supplies reusable proof/certificate recording and constant-instantiation rules, not a second factorization or point-count algorithm.

For every smooth projective geometrically connected curve C/F_q of genus g and r≥1, |#C(F_{q^r})−(q^r+1)|≤2g q^{r/2}; for a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d>0, |N_r−(1+q^{dr})|≤Σ_{i=1}^{2d−1} b_i q^{ir/2}. Dimension zero is handled separately. Export the actual rational-point/cohomology comparison and geometric Frobenius sign convention. This is the supplier contract for a general point-count certificate, not a theorem inferred from the elliptic Hasse bound or an affine hyperelliptic sum. Scope this request to the general point-bound component proposed below. The existing elliptic root-table certificate uses its elliptic suppliers, and the affine hyperelliptic estimate uses FF.2; neither acquires a compulsory WC.5 prerequisite from this request.

gaps.title: General-model certificate comparison
gaps.detail: WC.5 states the required all-extension bounds, but the accepted FF.3 certificate prototype is for affine y²=f and Schoof is elliptic. gaps.title: Schoof prime-growth estimate and instantiated operational cost model
gaps.detail: Schoof §5 invokes a weak prime-number theorem to obtain O(log q) auxiliary primes of size O(log q). The pinned citations and the precise CN.0 supplier stage do not provide that quantitative prime-product estimate. Import it from its owner or prove/source its exact elementary Chebyshev version, excluding char(F), before closing this cost target. CN.0 is an explicit requested bit/randomness model, not an already exported operation counter; the listed polynomial-time cost remains a target-level contract against that model, not a theorem about an arbitrary supplied count field.

imports.statement: A list L = ((g1, s1), …, (gt, st)) is a square-free decomposition of f ∈ F[X] (IsSquarefreeDecomposition f L) if each gi is monic, of positive degree and square-free, each si ≥ 1, the gi are pairwise coprime, the si are pairwise distinct, and f = ∏ gi^si. For monic f this holds exactly when L lists, for each multiplicity s occurring in the factorization of f, the pair (∏_{h : v_h(f) = s} h, s) once; in particular it is unique up to order.

imports.statement: Let I be an ideal of a commutative ring R, f ∈ R[X] monic, and g0, h0 monic with f ≡ g0 h0 (mod I) and ḡ0, h̄0 coprime in (R/I)[X]. Then for every k ≥ 1 there are monic g, h ∈ R[X] with deg g = deg g0, g ≡ g0 and h ≡ h0 (mod I), and f ≡ g h (mod I^k R[X]).
imports.why: Accepted parent FF.3 owner, reused without a duplicate declaration.

imports.statement: Let R be I-adically complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete I R), f ∈ R[X] monic, and f̄ = g0 h0 in (R/I)[X] with g0, h0 monic and coprime. Then there is a unique pair (g, h) of monic polynomials in R[X] with ḡ = g0, h̄ = h0 and f = g h. (For R = ℤ_p, I = (p) this is Milne's Theorem 7.33 over ℤ_p; for R = 𝔽_q⟦t⟧ over the power series ring.)

imports.statement: Let p be prime, k ≥ 1, f ∈ ℤ[X] monic and f mod p = g0 h0 in 𝔽_p[X] with g0, h0 monic and coprime. Then there is a unique pair (g, h) of monic polynomials in (ℤ/p^kℤ)[X] reducing to (g0, h0) modulo p with f mod p^k = g h. This is the form used by factoring algorithms over ℤ.

imports.statement: For n ≥ 1 and b ≠ 0, the number Π_F(n; b) of monic irreducible polynomials of degree n with constant coefficient b satisfies |n (q − 1) Π_F(n; b)/q^n − 1| ≤ 3 q^{1 − n/2}. Hence Π_F(n; b) = q^n/((q − 1) n) (1 + O(q^{1 − n/2})) with absolute implied constant 3, the statement Bary-Soroker–Koukoulopoulos–Kozma use in the proof of Lemma 3.2 (item 130 of the extraction), citing Rosen, Theorem 4.8.
imports.why: Accepted parent FF.3 owner, reused without a duplicate declaration.

imports.statement: For a finite field F with q elements and n ∈ ℕ, irreducibleCount F n = Π_F(n) is the number of monic irreducible polynomials of degree n in F[X] (Shoup's Π_F(ℓ); for F = 𝔽_p it is Bary-Soroker–Koukoulopoulos–Kozma's π_p(k)). Its package is Gauss's formula Σ_{d|n} d Π_F(d) = q^n, the Möbius formula n Π_F(n) = Σ_{d|n} μ(d) q^{n/d}, and the bounds (q^n − 2q^{n/2})/n ≤ Π_F(n) ≤ q^n/n and q^n ≤ 2n Π_F(n) (n ≥ 1).
imports.why: Accepted parent FF.3 owner, reused without a duplicate declaration.

imports.statement: For a finite field F, n ∈ ℕ and b ∈ F, irreducibleCountWithConstantCoeff F n b is the number of f ∈ monicIrreducibles F n with f(0) = b (for F = 𝔽_p and b ≠ 0, the count of I_p in Bary-Soroker–Koukoulopoulos–Kozma's proof of Lemma 3.2).

Assign naive elliptic point counts, root-table certificates and Schoof to a point-count component using their elliptic suppliers; keep the affine hyperelliptic bound on its exact FF.2 supplier. Assign general all-extension curve/variety bounds and their model/certificate comparison to the point-bound component importing WC.5. Remove the compulsory all-FF.2 algorithm edge. CN.1 replaces its duplicate polynomial-factorization-over-finite-fields target with the elementary component’s square-free, DDF, Cantor–Zassenhaus and Berlekamp correctness/cost imports, retaining implementation/refinement obligations; it must not import the whole point-bound stage. Merely substituting WC.5 for FF.2 on an unsplit FF.3 stage would preserve the cohomological obstruction. FA.7 imports the elementary factorization component and the relevant point-count certificates, retaining place enumeration, Riemann–Roch computations, ray characters, conductors/local completions, its other certificate exports, and L-polynomial assembly/functional-equation checks. Counts through r=g determine the curve zeta numerator only for a smooth projective geometrically connected genus-g curve, using Newton identities and the normalized functional equation; this does not replace arbitrary Artin/ramified L-polynomial computations. Split FF.4’s elementary constructions (direct FF.0/FF.1 inputs) from bound-dependent applications (their exact FF.2/WC suppliers), allowing a specific FF.3 algorithm import when a consumer needs it. FF.5 packages each exact supplying component. Move the elementary accepted monic-polynomials-of-degree carrier from its present FF.2 placement to FF.0 during assembly, updating parentStageId and all incoming references consistently without duplicating the declaration. Keep current stable node ids until the authorized component/census moves are registered and applied; then recompute depths. No stage split or foreign-file change is applied by this packet.
